text:
maria: Heads up — ran a 4h perf sweep on eu-west + us-central queue mixing. Found an odd tail increase when we do cross-zone batch synthesis.

alex: can you paste the numbers?

maria: baseline local-only batching p50/p95/p99 = 45ms / 120ms / 320ms. With opportunistic cross-zone merge enabled p50/p95/p99 = 46ms / 160ms / 580ms.

vikram: that's pretty bad at the tail. Did you correlate with kernel swaps?

maria: yes — spikes line up with kernel handoffs for quantized variants. When a merged batch contains a mix of q4/kbit and fp16 requests we force a kernel swap and flush caches.

sasha: ugh. so the runtime loads a different kernel and invalidates warm KV caches?

maria: exactly. Profiling shows ~35ms spent in kernel relocation + 120ms of stalled queue while KV access warms. Stack trace snippet: 
```
runtime: select_kernel(model=redwood-7b-q4, preferred=fast-attn)
loader: unload_kernel(fp16_impl)
kv_cache: missing_prefetch -> load_shard(0)
batcher: stall waiting for kernel_load
```

alex: any config we can tweak short term?

maria: two knobs: 1) prefer strict affinity unless token_budget_flex > X. 2) increase KV prefetch window for cross-zone merges so shard hits are primed.

jordan: what's token_budget_flex?r

maria: it's the percent of missing tokens allowed to be filled by remote shards when merging (defaults to 0). I tested at 12% and 25%. 12% reduced throughput loss but still had tail spikes. 25% eliminated smaller merges but amplified the kernel swap frequency.

vikram: seems like a tradeoff: larger token flex avoids tiny local batches but increases heterogeneity leading to more kernel variants per batch.

sasha: could we gate kernel_variant by batch composition? e.g., if >80% q4 prefer q4 kernel and convert rest via fast-cast instead of swapping entire kernel.

maria: we tried cast-up micro-op but hit numerical degradation on some eval prompts (short-term). Also adds overhead.

perf-bot: automated note — captured perf flame graphs attached to the thread (link: https://perf.redwood.internal/scan/1908765432).

alex: what's the cost of adding a small waiting window to let batcher aggregate more homogeneous requests locally? say 4–6ms.

maria: with a 5ms local hold, p95 improved back to 130ms and p99 to 310ms. But overall throughput dropped ~3% during peak.

jordan: 3% throughput trade for 50% tail improvement seems ok for latency-sensitive routes. We should differentiate by route SLA.

vikram: propose policy: 
- keep default regional affinity ON
- allow opportunistic cross-zone fills only if: token_budget_flex <= 10% AND dominant_variant_fraction >= 0.85
- add KV prefetch for shards expected to be hit by a merged batch
- add a 5ms local aggregation delay when predicted batch heterogeneity > 0.15

sasha: config proto (pseudo):
```
batching:
  local_hold_ms: 5
  crosszone:
    enabled: true
    token_budget_flex: 0.10
    dominant_variant_threshold: 0.85
  kv_prefetch: true
```

maria: I also ran microbenchmarks of kernel swap cost across models: average swap cost (q4 <-> fp16) = 28ms kernel load + ~50ms warm KV penalty for cold shards.

alex: can we pre-warm kernels based on traffic pattern predictions? e.g., on a spill event pre-load partner kernels into spare gpu memory LRU slot.

maria: memory constraints make that risky for 32GB GPUs but might work for larger hosts. We could opportunistically pre-load when spare memory > 6GB and predicted merge probability > 0.6.

vikram: add heuristic: if future window predicted cross-zone merges > 0.7, prefetch kcache + kernel into shadow slot. But need safe eviction policy.

jordan: action items: 
- maria: add the proposed policy changes to the experiment branch (batchheuristics/geo-synthesis) and a flag to toggle pre-warm.
- sasha: prototype dominant_variant_fraction calc in batcher and fast-cast fallback.
- alex: run a 24h canary with 20% traffic on eu-west and us-central with new config. Collect p50/p95/p99 + kernel_swap_count + kv_miss_rate.

maria: I'll attach the perf graphs and test plan to the PR. Quick checklist I pushed: 
- testplan.md (smoke + load)
- flamegraphs + sample logs
- policy proto

perf-bot: canary scheduled: 2026-03-18T03:00Z on 20% traffic.

alex: thanks — let's aim to reconvene after the canary and see if pre-warm wins vs local_hold. :thumbsup:

sasha: noted. I'll try to keep the fast-cast error delta under 0.5% on eval set.

maria: thanks all. I'll post the PR link here when ready.
